lead: For most people the best Abu Dhabi day trip from Dubai is the €45 Premium Full-Day Sightseeing Tour: hotel pickup, a guided visit inside the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, the Corniche, Emirates Palace and a Louvre photo stop, with a guide in one of five languages. Only want the mosque? The 5-hour half-day tour costs the same and gives you the afternoon back.

What decides the booking is what you actually go inside. Most tours from €30 show you the Louvre, Qasr Al Watan and Ferrari World from the kerb. If the Louvre Abu Dhabi matters, book one of the three tours with the museum ticket included (€57–85). For the presidential palace interior, pick a tour with Qasr Al Watan entry.
Below, 10 tours compared on price, length, entries included, lunch, group size and the mosque dress code, with a side-by-side table and filters for Louvre, palace and budget trips.

review: This is the default Abu Dhabi day trip, and for good reason. For €45 you get hotel pickup in Dubai, a mosque entry ticket and a licensed guide inside Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque for about 1.5 hours, then the Corniche, Emirates Palace and a photo stop at the Louvre Abu Dhabi. That is the same price as the half-day mosque-only tour at #2, so if you have a full day, this is simply more Abu Dhabi for the money.

The interesting part is the Premium option. It adds entry to Qasr Al Watan, the presidential palace (1.5 hours), and the Observation Deck at 300 on the 74th floor of Etihad Towers. Note that guides are not allowed inside Qasr Al Watan, so the palace is self-guided, and if it closes for a presidential event the Louvre takes its place. If Etihad Towers closes, the Founder's Memorial replaces it.

Catches: lunch is an add-on, men need to arrive dressed for the mosque (shoulders, knees and tattoos covered, no clothing provided), and the day runs 9–10 hours. The listing warns against Friday tours if you fly that day. Dubai Airport pickup is only from the Holiday Inn Dubai Airport Hotel.

review: If the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque is the only reason you are going to Abu Dhabi, this is the efficient way to do it. The 5 hours include the drive, roughly 1.5 hours each way, so you are back in Dubai with half a day left for something else.

What you pay for is the time inside: 1.5 hours with a licensed guide in the mosque itself, pointing out the marble mosaics, the crystal chandeliers and the hand-knotted carpet in the main prayer hall, and finding the photo spots. Women can borrow an abaya and headscarf if that option is chosen; men must turn up with shoulders, legs and knees covered, as no clothing is provided.
The catch is value: at €45 it costs the same as the full-day tour at #1, which adds the Corniche, Emirates Palace and a Louvre photo stop. Book this one for the time saved, not the price.

review: This is the tour for people who want to see as much of Abu Dhabi as possible in one day, even if mostly through the window. For €49 you get pickup in Dubai, a 1.5-hour guided visit at the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, 20 minutes at the Heritage Village, a 30-minute break at Marina Mall, a drive across Yas Island with a 20-minute Ferrari World photo stop, and photo stops or drive-bys at the Louvre, Emirates Palace, Qasr Al Watan, Etihad Towers, the Founder's Memorial and the Corniche. The description ends the day at the Dates Market.

Against its neighbours it is not the bargain. The City Tour at #6 costs €30 for a similar loop with 2 hours at the mosque and its own Ferrari World stop, and the Premium Full-Day at #1 costs about €5 less with guides in five languages and a Qasr Al Watan option. What this one does better: Yas Island and Ferrari World are fixed in the itinerary (optional on #5), the mosque visit is guided (on #5 guides may wait outside when it is busy), and with 955 reviews at 4.8 it has a far longer record than #6's 114, with guests scoring the guide and transport 4.9 each.

Catches: nothing apart from the mosque is an entry. Lunch is not included, so the Marina Mall break is where you eat. Women can use an abaya and scarf at no charge; men need to arrive dressed for the mosque, with no sleeveless shirts, as clothing for men is not included. The Heritage Village is closed in Ramadan, luggage and large bags are not allowed, and at 10 hours the day leaves little room for evening plans.

review: A focused, respectful product: transport from your Dubai hotel to Friday (Jumu'ah) prayer at the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque and back. Pickup starts at 10:30, prayer begins at 12:45, and the whole trip takes about 5 hours.

On the drive the guide gives commentary on the UAE and the mosque. At the mosque you have 1.5 hours of free time to make wudu, hear the khutbah and pray, then a few minutes to take in the courtyards before regrouping. Groups are capped at 12.

The listing is clear that this is for Muslim guests attending prayer, not a sightseeing visit. Men need long trousers and covered shoulders; women need loose clothing covering arms and legs and a headscarf.

review: Most Abu Dhabi tours drive past Emirates Palace. This one takes you inside for an hour, with the hotel's signature 23K gold-flaked Palace Cappuccino and a slice of cake included. Around it sit a guided Grand Mosque visit with entry, the Heritage Village, the Corniche, a Qasr Al Watan photo stop and a drive past Yas Island.

At €179 it is by far the priciest option, and it is a new listing without guest reviews yet. What you pay for is pace and setting: fewer stops, a proper sit-down at the palace, and the choice of a private tour with your own vehicle and guide.

Practicalities: bring your passport or Emirates ID, dress smart casual for Emirates Palace (no beachwear or flip-flops), and plan for lunch at your own expense. On Fridays the mosque closes to visitors from 11:30 to 14:30, so the itinerary is rearranged.

guide.h2: Abu Dhabi Day Trips from Dubai Compared Side by Side
guide.html:
The ten tours on the details that decide the day: price, length, how long you get at the Grand Mosque, whether the Louvre and Qasr Al Watan are entries or just photo stops, lunch and group size. All ten include pickup in Dubai (one uses a meeting point for some outer areas) and free cancellation up to 24 hours before. Prices are adult from-prices in euros for a normal date.

Three numbers matter most. The full day at #1 and the half day at #2 cost the same €45, so the half day only makes sense if you need the time. Getting inside the Louvre adds €13–24 over #1 (€57 at #4, €69 at #3). And the cheapest full days at €30 (#5, #6) work out at about €3 per hour of tour, but their palace and Louvre visits are mostly photo stops unless you buy an option. The landmark loop at #7 costs €19 more than #6 for a similar route: the extra buys a fixed Yas Island stop and a much longer review record, not more entries.

• First visit, one day, best all-round: Premium Full-Day Tour at €45; choose the Premium option for Qasr Al Watan and the Etihad Towers deck.
  • Only the mosque, half a day: Mosque Half-Day, 5 hours door to door.
  • Louvre Abu Dhabi tour from Dubai: Grand Mosque & Louvre for 2 full hours at each, or the small-group version (max 10, more photo stops) for €11 less.
  • Tightest budget: Budget Full-Day Tour or City Tour with Optional Lunch, both about €30; the second picks up at Port Rashid and Dubai Harbour, so it suits cruise passengers.
  • Most landmarks in one day, Yas Island included: Abu Dhabi Tour with Yas Island Stop at €49, a guided mosque visit plus a dozen photo stops and drive-bys.
  • Museum lovers: Mosque, Zayed Museum & Louvre, three entries for €85. For the Dubai side, see our guide to Dubai museums.
  • Friday prayer: Friday Prayer at the Grand Mosque, Fridays only, for Muslim guests.
  • Luxury, slow pace: Emirates Palace Coffee Tour, with an hour inside the palace hotel.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Dress Code, Fridays and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
The mosque dress code

Every tour enforces it, and failing it means no entry. Men: long trousers and tops that cover the shoulders; no shorts or sleeveless shirts. Women: long, loose clothing covering arms and legs, nothing see-through, and the hair covered. Tattoos must be covered. Most tours lend women an abaya and headscarf; none include clothing for men (#6 can arrange it). If you forget, traditional clothing can be bought at the mosque.

Fridays, holidays and flight days

The Emirates Palace coffee tour's listing notes the mosque closes to visitors on Fridays from 11:30 to 14:30, so its itinerary is rearranged; check the order of stops on any Friday tour. Entry is not guaranteed on Islamic holidays, and Qasr Al Watan can close without notice for presidential events (most tours then swap in the Louvre). Several listings warn against booking on the day you fly: the drive is about 1–1.5 hours each way and traffic can delay drop-off.

What costs extra

Lunch is not in any from-price here: it is either an option or a break at your own cost. The Louvre is a photo stop unless the tour includes entry (#3, #4, #8), and Qasr Al Watan entry comes only as an option, on #1 (Premium) and #6. Tips are never included, and luggage is either not allowed or charged.

Combining Abu Dhabi with the rest of your trip

For Ferrari World, Warner Bros. World or SeaWorld, a park ticket with a mosque visit and transfer is covered in our Dubai and Abu Dhabi theme parks guide. Abu Dhabi tours run all day, so keep the evening light, or save your desert safari and Burj Khalifa visit for other days. For Dubai's own sights, see our Dubai city tours; for another full-day trip out of the city, Musandam tours from Dubai.

faqs.q: What is the best Abu Dhabi day trip from Dubai?
faqs.a: For most people the Premium Full-Day Sightseeing Tour at €45: hotel pickup, a guided visit inside the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, the Corniche, Emirates Palace and a Louvre photo stop, with guides in five languages. Its Premium option adds Qasr Al Watan and the Etihad Towers deck.

faqs.q: Which Abu Dhabi tours from Dubai include Louvre entry?
faqs.a: Three: the Grand Mosque & Louvre Full-Day (€69, 2 hours inside), the small-group Grand Mosque & Louvre tour (€57, about 2 hours, max 10 people) and the Mosque, Zayed Museum & Louvre tour (€85). On the others the Louvre is a photo stop or not visited.

faqs.q: How long is an Abu Dhabi day trip from Dubai?
faqs.a: The drive takes about 1–1.5 hours each way. A mosque-only half day takes about 5 hours door to door; full-day tours run 7–10 hours including transfers.

faqs.q: What should I wear to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque?
faqs.a: Men: long trousers and covered shoulders, no shorts or sleeveless tops. Women: loose clothing covering arms and legs, nothing see-through, and a headscarf. Tattoos must be covered. Most tours lend women an abaya; no tour includes clothing for men in the price.

faqs.q: Is lunch included on Abu Dhabi tours from Dubai?
faqs.a: Not in the from-price of any tour here. Some offer lunch as an option (an international buffet, Al Khayma Heritage Restaurant or a checkout add-on); on the others there is a lunch break at your own cost.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Grand Mosque on a Friday?
faqs.a: Yes, but one listing notes it closes to visitors from 11:30 to 14:30 on Fridays, so tours change the order of stops. Muslim travellers can join the Friday Prayer tour, which is timed for Jumu'ah at 12:45.

faqs.q: Can I combine Abu Dhabi sightseeing with Ferrari World?
faqs.a: Several tours here include a Ferrari World photo stop only; #6 and #7 build it into the base itinerary. For a day trip with a park ticket and the mosque, see our theme parks guide.

methodology: We compared 10 bookable Abu Dhabi day trips from Dubai, from mosque-only half days to full-day city tours, a landmark loop with Yas Island, Louvre and museum days, a Friday prayer trip and an Emirates Palace coffee tour. Each was scored on adult price, tour length, time at the Grand Mosque, which sights are entries and which are photo stops (Louvre, Qasr Al Watan, Etihad Towers, Emirates Palace), lunch, pickup, group size, languages and dress code. Prices are live listing from-prices for a normal date; ratings come from verified guest reviews.
